finding: tests/test_signal_search.py:248 The public redaction boundary is not asserted on returned payloads.
rationale: The canonical detector path can persist arbitrary detector-result keys, and search returns the projection payload verbatim; the tests only prove that private_context is not indexed and never assert the returned key/value shape, so a regression that copies raw signal fields into payload_json while retaining the public search_fields allowlist is reachable and would evade the suite.

evidence.output: Lines 32-56 seed signal-alpha with top-level private_context='classified-swordfish'; lines 42 and 67 use previews containing only vendor/amount, so no credential-bearing nested fixture exists. Lines 239-256 assert selected returned values but never assert the complete item key set or absence/redaction of sensitive values. Lines 281-289 assert matched_on and that searching for 'classified-swordfish' returns no items, which covers indexing only.

Lines 654-676 construct each canonical signal as {**result, ...} and append it after credential text redaction; lines 738-740 write those rows to evidence/signals.jsonl. Arbitrary non-public detector-result keys are therefore reachable inputs to the projection.

_signal_projection.py lines 218-231 currently protect the boundary by allowlisting _PUBLIC_SIGNAL_FIELDS and recursively sanitizing public signal/metadata before serializing payload_json, while lines 232-245 build search_fields separately. search.py lines 141-151 deserialize payload_json, add only matched_on/query_score, and return it. Thus changing payload construction to include raw signal keys would leak them without making private_context searchable, exactly the regression the existing assertions miss.

Acceptance-criterion disposition 1 promises that the deterministic seam test_projection_filters_every_structured_facet_without_mutating_evidence 'checks ... allowlisted result shape'; the locked test asserts individual required fields but not an allowlisted/exact shape.
